# mypy plugin features

<!-- Generated by `plugin_features_doc.py` from the plugin hook docstrings, do not edit. -->

## App registry

### Narrow `apps.get_model()` to the referenced model

With literal arguments, the model class is returned instead of `type[Any]`.

```python
reveal_type(apps.get_model("myapp.Book"))  # type[Book]
apps.get_model("myapp.Missing")  # error: Could not match lazy reference with any model  [misc]
```

Migration `apps` (`StateApps`) keep `type[Any]`, since their models are historical.

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/apps.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/apps.py) · Hook: `resolve_model_for_get_model`

## Auth user model

### Resolve `get_user_model()`, `request.user` and other auth APIs to `AUTH_USER_MODEL`

```python
# settings.py: AUTH_USER_MODEL = "myapp.MyUser"
reveal_type(get_user_model())  # type[MyUser]
reveal_type(request.user)  # MyUser | AnonymousUser
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/auth.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/auth.py) · Hook: `get_user_model`

## Choices

### Narrow the value and label types of `Choices` enums

`choices`, `values`, `labels`, `value` and `label` follow the enum definition,
and `__empty__` adds `None` to the values.

```python
class Gender(models.TextChoices):
    MALE = "M", "Male"
    __empty__ = "(Undeclared)"

reveal_type(Gender.choices)  # list[tuple[str | None, str]]
reveal_type(Gender.MALE.label)  # str
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/choices.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/choices.py) · Hook: `transform_into_proper_attr_type`

## Field lookups

### Type-check lookups passed to `filter()`, `get()`, `exclude()` and friends

Also covers `get_or_create()`, `update_or_create()` and the async variants.

```python
Book.objects.filter(nope=1)  # error: Cannot resolve keyword 'nope' into field. Choices are: id, title  [misc]
Book.objects.get(id=Book())  # error: Incompatible type for lookup 'id': (got "Book", expected "str | int")  [misc]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/orm_lookups.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/orm_lookups.py) · Hook: `typecheck_queryset_filter`

## Forms

### Allow combining forms whose nested `Meta` classes differ

A form's `Meta` is typed as `Any`, so inheriting from several forms isn't reported as an incompatible definition.

```python
class CompositeForm(ArticleForm, CategoryForm): ...  # no error
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/forms.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/forms.py) · Hook: `make_meta_nested_class_inherit_from_any`

## HTTP requests

### Report mutations of immutable `QueryDict`s such as `request.GET`

```python
request.GET["page"] = "2"  # error: This QueryDict is immutable.  [misc]
params = request.GET.copy()
params["page"] = "2"  # OK
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/request.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/request.py) · Hook: `check_querydict_is_mutable`

## Managers

### Resolve `QuerySet` methods on managers built by `from_queryset()` and `as_manager()`

Custom methods are bound to the model, and built-in ones return your queryset class.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    objects = models.Manager.from_queryset(BookQuerySet)()

reveal_type(Book.objects.filter(id=1))  # BookQuerySet[Book, Book]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/managers.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/managers.py) · Hook: `resolve_manager_method`

### Create a manager class for a module-level `Manager.from_queryset()`

```python
BookManager = models.Manager.from_queryset(BookQuerySet)

class Book(models.Model):
    objects = BookManager()

reveal_type(Book.objects)  # ManagerFromBookQuerySet[Book]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/managers.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/managers.py) · Hook: `create_new_manager_class_from_from_queryset_method`

### Type `QuerySet.as_manager()` as a manager with the queryset's methods

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    objects = BookQuerySet.as_manager()

reveal_type(Book.objects)  # ManagerFromBookQuerySet[Book]
reveal_type(Book.objects.published())  # BookQuerySet[Book, Book]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/managers.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/managers.py) · Hook: `add_as_manager_to_queryset_class`

## Many-to-many relations

### Add the related model's manager methods to `ManyToManyField` managers

Applies to both sides of the relation.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    authors = models.ManyToManyField(Author)

reveal_type(Book().authors.active())  # AuthorQuerySet[Author, Author], from Author's default manager
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/manytomany.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/manytomany.py) · Hook: `refine_many_to_many_related_manager`

## Many-to-one relations

### Add the related model's manager methods to reverse `ForeignKey` managers

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    author = models.ForeignKey(Author, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="books")
    objects = BookQuerySet.as_manager()

reveal_type(Author().books.published())  # BookQuerySet[Book, Book]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/manytoone.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/manytoone.py) · Hook: `refine_many_to_one_related_manager`

## Model classes

### Report `objects` and `DoesNotExist` accessed where Django doesn't add them

Django adds `objects` to concrete models only, and `DoesNotExist` and friends to `Model` subclasses only.

```python
def count(model: type[models.Model]) -> None:
    model.objects.count()  # error: "type[Model]" has no attribute "objects"  [attr-defined]
```

Set `strict_model_abstract_attrs = false` to allow it, at your own risk: `count(models.Model)` fails at runtime.

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/models.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/models.py) · Hook: `MetaclassAdjustments.adjust_model_class`

### Add the attributes Django generates on model classes

Such as `id` and `pk`, `<fk>_id`, managers, reverse relations, `get_<field>_display()` and `DoesNotExist`.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    publisher = models.ForeignKey(Publisher, on_delete=models.CASCADE)

reveal_type(Book().publisher_id)  # int
reveal_type(Publisher().book_set)  # RelatedManager[Book]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/models.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/models.py) · Hook: `process_model_class`

### Infer `is_staff`, `is_active` and `is_superuser` of user models as `bool`

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/models.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/models.py) · Hook: `set_auth_user_model_boolean_fields`

## Model fields

### Infer the value type of model fields from their arguments

`null=True` adds `None`, and related fields resolve their target model, even given as a string.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    subtitle = models.CharField(max_length=100, null=True)
    publisher = models.ForeignKey("Publisher", on_delete=models.CASCADE)

reveal_type(Book().subtitle)  # str | None
reveal_type(Book().publisher)  # Publisher
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/fields.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/fields.py) · Hook: `transform_into_proper_return_type`

## QuerySets

### Infer the model of a manager instantiated in a model body

So `objects = BookManager()` needs no annotation.

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    objects = BookManager()

reveal_type(Book.objects)  # BookManager[Book]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `determine_proper_manager_type`

### Infer the row type returned by `QuerySet.values_list()`

Including `flat=True` and `named=True`.

```python
reveal_type(Book.objects.values_list("title", "pages").get())  # tuple[str, int]
reveal_type(Book.objects.values_list("title", flat=True).get())  # str
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `extract_proper_type_queryset_values_list`

### Infer the output type of a `Func` expression from its `output_field`

```python
book = Book.objects.annotate(raw=Substr("title", 1, 10, output_field=BinaryField())).get()
reveal_type(book.raw)  # bytes | memoryview[int]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `reparameterize_func_output_field`

### Add the names given to `QuerySet.annotate()` and `alias()` to the model type

```python
reveal_type(Book.objects.annotate(n=Count("id")).get().n)  # int
Book.objects.annotate(title=F("id"))  # error: Attribute "title" already defined on "Book"  [no-redef]
```

`alias()` names are typed as instance attributes too, although Django doesn't set them.

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `extract_proper_type_queryset_annotate`

### Keep annotations through custom `QuerySet` methods returning `WithAnnotations`

```python
class BookQuerySet(models.QuerySet[_M]):
    def with_price(self) -> "BookQuerySet[WithAnnotations[_M, PriceDict]]": ...

book = Book.objects.annotate(n=Count("id")).with_price().get()
reveal_type(book.price)  # int
reveal_type(book.n)  # int
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `merge_annotations_from_custom_method`

### Keep the `lookup` and `to_attr` of `Prefetch()` as literal types

So a `Prefetch` stored in a variable still adds its `to_attr` in `prefetch_related()`.

```python
tags = Prefetch("tags", Tag.objects.all(), to_attr="tag_list")
reveal_type(tags)  # Prefetch[Literal['tags'], QuerySet[Tag, Tag], Literal['tag_list']]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `specialize_prefetch_type`

### Type-check `QuerySet.prefetch_related()` and add `Prefetch(to_attr=...)` attributes

```python
reveal_type(book.tag_list)  # list[Tag]
```

### Report invalid `QuerySet.select_related()` lookups

Lookups must follow foreign keys or one-to-one relations.

```python

```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `validate_select_related`


### Report unknown fields in `QuerySet.defer()` and `only()`

### Report unknown fields in `QuerySet.distinct()`

Fields resolve like in `order_by()`, without the `-` prefix.

```python
Book.objects.distinct("-title")  # error: Cannot resolve keyword '-title' into field. Choices are: ...  [misc]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `validate_distinct`

### Report unknown or non-concrete fields in `QuerySet.update()`

```python
Book.objects.update(nope=1)  # error: Book has no field named 'nope'  [misc]

```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/querysets.py) · Hook: `validate_update`


## Saving models

### Type-check the `update_fields` of `Model.save()` and `Model.asave()`

```python
book.save(update_fields=["nope"])  # error: Book has no field named 'nope'  [misc]
book.save(update_fields=["id"])  # error: "save()" does not support primary key fields. Got "id"  [misc]
```

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/save.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/save.py) · Hook: `validate_save_update_fields`

## Settings

### Infer `django.conf.settings` attribute types from your settings module

Falling back to Django's defaults.

```python
reveal_type(settings.BASE_DIR)  # Path
settings.NOT_EXISTING  # error: 'Settings' object has no attribute 'NOT_EXISTING'  [misc]
```

Set `strict_settings = false` to type settings only created at runtime as `Any` instead of reporting them.

Source: [`mypy_django_plugin/transformers/settings.py`](../mypy_django_plugin/transformers/settings.py) · Hook: `get_type_of_settings_attribute`
